description: OIDC authorization request object bypass: send an unsigned request object (alg=none) that attempts to override authorization parameters (redirect_uri/scope). Expect Dex to reject or ignore the unsigned request object so it cannot influence the consumed authorization request semantics.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must not accept an unsigned (alg=none) OIDC request object such that attacker-controlled parameters are consumed without signature verification.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted an unsigned (alg=none) request object; attacker-controlled authorization parameters may be consumed without signature verification (I1).
Control authorization request did not reach a normal auth endpoint response; request-object test results may be inconclusive due to setup/connector issues.

description: Token exchange trust-anchor substitution: attempt token exchange using a subject_token that should not validate under the configured OIDC connector trust anchor (issuer/JWKS). Expect rejection; acceptance would indicate signature/issuer verification not applied to the consumed token semantics.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex token exchange must verify the upstream token against the configured connector issuer/JWKS; a forged token from an attacker-controlled issuer/JWKS must not be accepted.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control login did not succeed; token-exchange rejection/acceptance may be due to environment setup rather than proof verification behavior.
Dex accepted a subject_token that appears to be from an attacker-controlled issuer/JWKS; indicates missing or misapplied issuer/signature verification (I1).

description: Direct-endpoint attack: send an unsigned OIDC request object (alg=none) to the request-object test endpoint, attempting to get the server to accept and process attacker-controlled authorization parameters. This probes whether signature verification is applied to the same semantic request that is consumed.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: If Dex (or the fronting OIDC endpoint) accepts an unsigned request object, it may consume attacker-controlled parameters (redirect_uri/scope) without applying authenticity checks to the semantic request, violating proof integrity.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Unsigned request object must be rejected (or at least not lead to an authenticated session).
Even if the endpoint responds, it must not result in a logged-in identity via an unsigned request object.

description: Brokered-flow attack: attempt RFC8693 token exchange using a subject_token that is a JWT with alg=none (unsigned). Control is a normal password login to prove the client/session plumbing works; then attempt exchange with the forged token.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must not accept an unsigned JWT as a subject_token for token exchange; otherwise it is consuming semantic claims without applying authenticity checks to the same proof.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control: password login should succeed so token endpoint/client config is known-good (otherwise exchange failures are ambiguous).
Token exchange must reject an unsigned (alg=none) JWT subject_token.
Even if an HTTP response is returned, it must not mint an authenticated identity from the unsigned token.

description: Direct-endpoint attack: attempt to inject elevated scopes via an unsigned OIDC request object (alg=none). Secure behavior is explicit rejection or non-processing of the unsigned request object so attacker-controlled semantics are not consumed.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: If Dex accepts and processes an unsigned request object, it may consume attacker-controlled authorization semantics (scope/redirect_uri) without applying authenticity checks to the same semantic proof.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted an unsigned (alg=none) request object, indicating request semantics may be consumed without proof integrity verification.
Unsigned request object probe unexpectedly resulted in a valid authenticated session/userinfo response, suggesting consumed semantics were not bound to a verified proof.

description: Brokered-flow attack: perform a control token exchange using a legitimate subject_token, then attempt token exchange with a forged JWT that uses an issuer-like value intended to confuse trust anchoring (issuer substitution). Secure behavior is rejection of the forged token.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must verify the submitted subject_token against the configured OIDC connector trust anchor (issuer/JWKS). If it consumes claims from a token with a substituted issuer without verifying under the intended policy, proof integrity is violated.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control token exchange failed; cannot attribute attack-flow failures to proof-integrity enforcement vs setup issues.
Dex accepted a forged JWT with substituted issuer semantics during token exchange, suggesting consumed claims were not verified under the intended trust anchor.

description: Direct-endpoint attack: attempt to supply a request object JWT signed with an attacker-controlled key (untrusted) and see if Dex accepts/processes it. If accepted, Dex may be consuming attacker-controlled authorization semantics without verifying the proof under the intended trust anchor (I1). Includes a control request-object attempt to distinguish 'unsupported' from 'accepted'.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must not accept or process an untrusted-signed OIDC request object; signature verification (or explicit rejection) must apply to the same semantic authorization request that is consumed.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control password login failed; request-object results would be inconclusive due to environment/client misconfiguration.

oracle_checks.assertion: user_victim_pwd_http_status == 200 AND user_victim_pwd_entity_id is not None
oracle_checks.violation_description: Control identity verification failed; cannot establish baseline session identity.
Unsigned request object (alg=none) was accepted; Dex may be consuming authorization semantics without verifying proof integrity.
Request object signed with an untrusted key/algorithm was accepted; Dex may be consuming attacker-controlled authorization parameters without verifying the correct proof.

oracle_checks.assertion: user_victim_pwd_entity_id is not None AND user_victim_pwd_http_status == 200
oracle_checks.violation_description: Post-attack identity verification failed unexpectedly; potential session corruption or unintended side effects during request-object handling.

description: I2 replay test: attempt to redeem the same authorization code twice (one-time artifact reuse). Includes a control successful code exchange, then immediate replay of the same code.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: Authorization codes are one-time artifacts; the same code must not be accepted more than once for token issuance.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control authorization_code exchange did not succeed; replay result would be inconclusive (setup/flow failure).
Authorization code was accepted more than once (code replay succeeded), violating one-time artifact freshness.

description: I2 replay test: obtain refresh_token via password grant (if enabled), then attempt to reuse the old refresh_token after a successful refresh (rotation expected by default). Uses two identities to satisfy multi-identity requirement.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: If refresh token rotation is enabled (Dex default), an old refresh_token must not be accepted after it has been used to obtain a new token set.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Password grant control did not succeed; refresh rotation test is inconclusive (grant may be disabled by config).
Old refresh token was accepted after being used once (rotation/reuse protection failed), violating anti-replay freshness.

description: I2 time-claim enforcement on token exchange: perform a control token exchange with a valid subject_token, then attempt exchange with an expired subject_token (exp in the past). Requires connector_id and client auth; includes verify steps for both outcomes.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: Token exchange must reject expired upstream subject tokens; acceptance would indicate missing exp validation or replay acceptance beyond lifetime.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control token exchange did not succeed; expired-token rejection would be inconclusive (connector/grant/client auth misconfig).
Token exchange accepted an expired subject_token (exp in the past), violating freshness/anti-replay expectations.

description: I2: Attempt to reuse a refresh_token after explicit revocation (replay of a revoked artifact). Control: obtain refresh_token via password grant; Attack: revoke then attempt token exchange using the revoked refresh_token as subject_token.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: A revoked refresh_token must not be accepted for subsequent token exchange; otherwise revoked artifacts remain usable (replay beyond intended lifetime).

oracle_checks.assertion: user_alice_pwd_login_http_status >= 200 AND user_alice_pwd_login_http_status < 400 AND user_alice_pwd_refresh_token is not None
oracle_checks.violation_description: Control failed: could not obtain refresh_token; cannot evaluate replay-after-revoke behavior.
Revocation endpoint behaved unexpectedly (5xx); test inconclusive.
Revoked refresh_token was accepted in token exchange (replay of revoked artifact).

description: I2 anti-replay: redeem an authorization code once, then attempt to redeem the same code again after a fresh re-auth/login (different identity) to detect any cache/session-based replay acceptance.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: Authorization codes are one-time artifacts; a previously redeemed code must not be accepted again even if a new user session is established.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control failed: initial authorization_code exchange did not succeed; cannot attribute replay outcome to anti-replay enforcement.
Authorization code replay succeeded after re-auth; one-time code was accepted more than once (anti-replay failure).

description: I2 freshness: obtain a Dex-issued ID token, exchange it for a new token (control), then revoke the exchanged session token and attempt to exchange the same original subject_token again to see if revocation/invalidations are enforced for downstream-issued artifacts.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: After revoking a session derived from a subject_token, the system should not allow continued reuse of the same subject_token to mint fresh sessions if revocation is intended to terminate that credential's effective lifetime.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control failed: initial token exchange did not succeed; cannot interpret replay-after-revocation behavior.
Subject token reuse succeeded after revoking the derived session; indicates ineffective freshness/termination semantics for exchanged sessions.

description: I2 time-claim enforcement: perform a control token exchange using a valid subject_token, then attempt token exchange using an explicitly expired subject_token (exp in the past) to ensure exp is enforced.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: Token exchange must reject expired subject tokens; otherwise stale credentials can be replayed beyond their lifetime.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control failed: valid subject_token could not be exchanged; expired-token rejection cannot be attributed to freshness enforcement.
Expired subject_token was accepted in token exchange; indicates missing exp enforcement and allows replay beyond intended lifetime.

description: Test whether a token obtained via RFC8693 token exchange remains usable after explicit revocation (freshness/anti-replay). Control: successful exchange and userinfo. Attack: revoke the exchanged session_token, then attempt to use the revoked token to access /userinfo again; it should be rejected.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: A revoked (invalidated) exchanged session_token must not be accepted for subsequent resource access; otherwise revoked artifacts remain reusable beyond intended lifetime.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control failed: password login did not succeed, so token-exchange freshness test is inconclusive.
Control failed: token exchange did not succeed, so revocation/freshness test is inconclusive (could be connector/grant/client auth setup).
Control failed: exchanged token could not access userinfo before revocation; cannot attribute post-revocation behavior to freshness enforcement.
I2 violation: revoked exchanged session_token was still accepted for userinfo (revocation did not invalidate the artifact).

description: I3 attack: attempt to redeem an authorization code without client authentication (no client_secret) to test code-to-client binding and flow coherence.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Authorization codes must be bound to the initiating client; exchanging a code without client authentication must be rejected.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control authorization-code exchange or userinfo failed; cannot attribute attack outcome to flow-coherence enforcement.
Authorization code was redeemable without client authentication, indicating missing code-to-client binding (flow coherence violation).

description: I3 state_swap: start two parallel OIDC auth requests (victim vs attacker) with distinct state values, then attempt to complete the flow using the wrong state's authorization code redemption context. Expected: token redemption should fail (or at least not mint a token bound to the wrong session/state).
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Authorization code redemption must be bound to the initiating browser session/state; cross-session state swapping must not succeed.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control failed: victim could not redeem auth code; cannot attribute failures to state/session binding.
Flow coherence broken: attacker redeemed victim's authorization code (cross-session/state swap) successfully.

description: I3 pkce_skip hardening check: initiate an auth request that includes a request object indicating PKCE usage, then attempt to redeem the code without code_verifier. Expected secure behavior for this test: reject the exchange (non-200).
invariant_hypothesis: I3: If the authorization request indicates PKCE was used, the token endpoint should require the matching code_verifier; skipping it must not succeed.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control failed: PKCE exchange with verifier did not succeed; cannot interpret pkce_skip result.
Flow coherence weakened: code exchange succeeded without code_verifier even though PKCE was indicated.

description: I3 request-object parameter splicing: send an unsigned request object (alg=none) to attempt overriding critical authorization parameters (client_id/redirect_uri/state) and then attempt to redeem any resulting code. Expected: request object is rejected or ignored such that no attacker-controlled parameter splice succeeds.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: The authorization request must not accept unsigned request objects that allow parameter splicing/cross-session confusion.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control failed: normal code flow did not succeed; cannot interpret request-object behavior.
Unsigned request object was accepted; may enable parameter splicing and break flow coherence.

description: I3 cross-client code redemption: obtain an authorization code for client A, then attempt to redeem it while authenticating as a different client_id (client binding / azp coherence). Expected: redemption rejected (non-200) and no usable session token minted.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Authorization codes must be bound to the initiating client_id; redeeming a code under a different client context must fail to prevent cross-client splicing.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control authorization-code flow failed; cannot attribute later failures/successes to flow-coherence enforcement.
Authorization code was redeemable under a different client_id context (cross-client splicing).

description: I3 connector binding in RFC8693 token exchange: exchange a subject_token while specifying an incorrect connector_id (wrong upstream binding). Expected: exchange rejected (non-200). Includes a control exchange with the correct connector_id.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Token exchange must be bound to the intended upstream connector; specifying a different connector_id must not succeed with the same subject_token.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control password login failed; token-exchange results may be setup-related (password grant not enabled).
Control token exchange failed; cannot attribute attack exchange outcome to connector binding enforcement.
Token exchange succeeded even when bound to an incorrect connector_id (flow not coherently bound to upstream connector).

description: I3 state coherence under parallel flows: start two auth requests from different sessions using the SAME state value, then attempt to redeem the victim code in attacker context. Expected: redemption rejected (non-200) or at minimum not mint a token usable by attacker session.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Authorization responses must be bound to the initiating browser session; reusing state across sessions must not allow cross-session splicing of the code redemption step.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control victim code exchange failed; cannot attribute splice outcome to state/session binding enforcement.
Victim authorization code was redeemable in attacker session (cross-session splicing despite shared state).

description: I4 case_confusion: attempt to collapse two security-distinct principals that differ only by username case (Admin vs admin) into the same downstream subject via password grant mapping.
invariant_hypothesis: I4: If the upstream principal identifier is case-variant (e.g., preferred_username), Dex must not normalize/case-fold in a way that maps distinct principals to the same downstream identity_id.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Baseline failed: mechanism cannot distinguish principals
Case confusion: distinct principals (Admin vs admin) collapsed to the same downstream subject

description: I4 cross_protocol_identity_merge: authenticate one principal via password grant, then attempt to authenticate a different upstream principal via OIDC connector that could share the same email; ensure Dex does not merge them into one downstream identity.
invariant_hypothesis: I4: A user authenticated via password connector and a different user authenticated via OIDC connector must not be merged solely due to shared email/preferred_username; downstream identity_id must remain distinct across security-distinct upstream principals.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Baseline failed: mechanism cannot distinguish principals
Cross-protocol identity merge: password principal and exchanged OIDC principal collapsed into the same downstream subject

description: I4 type_confusion_groups: exchange two upstream tokens for distinct principals where groups claim differs only by JSON type (string vs array) and check for identity collapse.
invariant_hypothesis: I4: If Dex claim parsing/type coercion causes principal key material to be miscomputed, two distinct upstream principals could map to the same downstream identity.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Baseline failed: mechanism cannot distinguish principals
Type confusion in groups claim caused two distinct upstream principals to collapse into the same downstream identity

description: Attempt to escalate claims/permissions by performing RFC8693 token exchange requesting broader scopes than were originally authorized in the OIDC code flow (UpstreamIntent=limited scopes).
invariant_hypothesis: I5: A token obtained with limited scopes (openid email) must not be exchangeable into a token that carries additional claims/policies (e.g., groups/profile/federated:id) beyond the original upstream intent and broker policy.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Token exchange accepted and returned a token with groups claim even though original upstream intent did not request groups scope (scope escalation beyond UpstreamIntent).
Token exchange increased effective granted policies beyond what was present in the limited-scope session (authorization binding failure).

description: Attempt scope escalation via unsigned request object (alg=none): send an unsigned request object that injects broader scopes than intended, then verify whether resulting identity/claims/policies exceed the intended scope set.
invariant_hypothesis: I5: Dex must not honor attacker-controlled authorization parameters from an unsigned request object; effective permissions/claims must remain within intended scopes and broker policy.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex appears to accept/process an unsigned request object and returns group claims (or equivalent elevated authorization) despite only requesting openid email in the query, violating Authorization Binding.

description: Attempt to splice authorization context across principals: obtain a subject_token as user_alice, then perform token_exchange authenticated as the same client but attempt to validate that the resulting identity cannot become user_bob or gain bob-linked policies/claims.
invariant_hypothesis: I5: Token exchange must not allow effective permissions/identity to exceed the upstream intent bound to the subject_token principal; exchanging alice's subject_token must not yield bob's identity or bob-only entitlements.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control logins failed; token-exchange splice result would be inconclusive due to setup/grant misconfiguration.

oracle_checks.assertion: user_attacker_exchange_http_status >= 400 OR (user_attacker_exchange_entity_id == user_alice_pwd_entity_id AND user_attacker_exchange_entity_id != user_bob_pwd_entity_id)
oracle_checks.violation_description: Token exchange allowed cross-principal identity/authorization splicing (alice subject_token yielded bob identity or an unexpected accepted exchange).

description: Attempt to influence authorization context using id_token_hint and login_hint to obtain a code/token for a different principal than the authenticated user, potentially granting permissions beyond upstream intent.
invariant_hypothesis: I5: Authorization must be bound to the authenticated upstream principal; providing id_token_hint/login_hint must not cause Dex to issue tokens for a different user or with elevated entitlements.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control password logins failed; cannot evaluate hint-based authorization confusion.
Attacker session mapped to victim identity after using victim id_token_hint/login_hint, indicating authorization binding failure.

description: Attempt to use a revoked subject_token in token exchange to obtain a fresh token (authorization should not exceed the still-valid upstream intent; revoked artifacts should not be usable to mint new effective permissions).
invariant_hypothesis: I5: After revocation, the upstream authorization context should not be usable to mint new tokens/permissions via token exchange; otherwise effective permissions exceed upstream intent (revoked session).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control login failed; revocation/exchange results are inconclusive.
Token exchange succeeded using a revoked subject_token, potentially minting effective permissions beyond the revoked upstream intent.

description: Attempt cross-client audience escalation via token exchange: obtain a subject_token as client valence-test-client, then request an exchanged token for a different audience (audience:server:client_id:other-client) without any trustedPeers relationship. Secure behavior is rejection or no elevation of effective permissions/identity.
invariant_hypothesis: I5: Token exchange must not mint tokens for an unauthorized audience/client (or with elevated effective permissions) beyond what the upstream subject_token and broker policy allow; cross-client audience issuance should be rejected unless explicitly trusted.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control password login failed; token-exchange results would be inconclusive due to setup/grant configuration rather than authorization binding.
Dex accepted token exchange for an unauthorized cross-client audience without explicit trust, potentially violating authorization binding (I5).
Cross-audience token exchange resulted in elevated effective policies compared to the upstream intent/session, indicating authorization binding failure (I5).
Cross-audience token exchange changed the downstream principal identity, suggesting authorization context confusion beyond upstream intent (I5).
